# Meals and Overnight Hotels — NS-CARE-2026

Effective January 1, 2026. Owner: Customer Experience Operations. These are fictional Northstar Air service commitments for disrupted domestic travel, not universal legal rights. Assess meals, hotels, rebooking and refunds separately.

## 1. Coverage and definitions
Use the policy effective on the disruption date. A passenger asking about today's benefits should receive the current rule, while a historical claim uses the edition in force at that time.

### 1.1 Covered passengers
The passenger must hold a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary and be present at the affected airport. Protected rebooking is governed separately by NS-CONN-2026.

### 1.2 Airline-controlled causes and home metro
MECHANICAL, CREW_OPERATIONAL and AIRLINE_OPERATIONS are airline-controlled causes. WEATHER and ATC_EXTERNAL are uncontrollable. UNKNOWN and MIXED_PENDING are unresolved. Home metro means the passenger's verified metropolitan area of residence, not their payment address or departure airport.

## 2. Basic assistance
Explain the flight status, feasible recovery options and any information still needed. Discretionary assistance must be recorded as COURTESY rather than a standard entitlement. A service offer does not certify that it was delivered.

## 3. Meal vouchers
Meal eligibility depends on the waiting time and approved cause, independently of hotel eligibility.

### 3.1 Three-hour waiting threshold
Provide a meal voucher after at least three consecutive hours of waiting for onward travel due to a final approved airline-controlled cause. Mechanical, crew and airline-operations disruptions can qualify. Do not count the same waiting interval twice when offers change.

### 3.2 Meal exclusions
Weather-only and external air-traffic-control delays do not qualify for standard meal vouchers. If the cause is unconfirmed, meal eligibility requires review. Staff may separately authorize courtesy assistance.

## 4. Overnight accommodation
Determine eligibility before arranging or reimbursing a room. An overnight delay alone is insufficient.

### 4.1 Primary hotel eligibility
Northstar provides an approved hotel when all four conditions hold: a valid disrupted Northstar itinerary; a final approved MECHANICAL or AIRLINE_OPERATIONS cause; onward travel requiring an overnight wait at the affected airport; and a passenger away from their verified home metro area. All conditions are required together.

### 4.2 Overnight necessity
An overnight wait means no reasonable onward option can be completed without staying at the recovery station into the following calendar day. Use feasible flight options and boarding constraints. A late departure or device date change alone does not establish overnight necessity.

### 4.3 Home-city restriction
A passenger stranded at an airport within their own home metro area is not eligible for the standard hotel. This applies even if their trip began elsewhere. Missing residence information requires review.

### 4.4 Weather, external ATC and unresolved causes
Weather and external ATC disruptions do not qualify for standard hotel coverage. UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an investigation still in progress means NEEDS_REVIEW; do not promise payment or assume the cause is uncontrollable.

### 4.5 Crew scheduling coverage
A finalized CREW_OPERATIONAL disruption is excluded from the standard hotel commitment. Crew shortages and rotation problems do not qualify for a routine hotel in this edition, even when airline-controlled. A duty manager may authorize a COURTESY booking, but it is not a standard benefit. Mechanical and airline-operations disruptions can qualify when the overnight, away-from-home and valid-itinerary conditions in §4.1 hold.

### 4.6 Self-booked hotels and written authorization

### 4.7 Approved cause controls

# Connection Protection and Rebooking — NS-CONN-2026

Effective January 1, 2026. Owner: Customer Operations. This fictional Northstar Air policy covers domestic protected connections. It describes recovery eligibility; an eligible passenger still needs a confirmed seat before travel is arranged.

## 1. Protected connections
A missed connection and a refund are separate decisions. Use this policy for replacement travel and NS-REF-2026 for refunds. Hotel assistance is assessed separately under NS-CARE-2026.

### 1.1 Covered transportation
A protected itinerary has at least two domestic Northstar-operated flights on the same ticket and reservation, sold as one continuous journey. The first flight must be disrupted before the onward flight's boarding cutoff. Separate tickets, codeshares, interline travel and international itineraries are outside this policy; refer those passengers to a specialist.

### 1.2 Confirming a missed connection
Compare actual inbound gate arrival, required transfer time and the onward boarding cutoff. A delayed inbound flight does not prove a missed connection if onward boarding remains open. Missing or contradictory operational times require review.

## 2. Rebooking and passenger choice
Rebooking eligibility, an available offer and a confirmed ticket are different stages. Staff must explain which stage has actually been reached.

### 2.1 No-additional-fare rebooking
For a verified protected missed connection, Northstar offers the earliest available Northstar-operated itinerary to the original destination at no additional fare. This applies to weather and other uncontrollable causes as well as mechanical, crew and airline-operations disruptions. Seat availability must be confirmed; no particular departure time is guaranteed.

### 2.2 Available alternatives
Search feasible same-day service, later connections and then next-day travel, considering the passenger's documented needs. A search result or temporary seat hold is not a confirmed reservation. External-carrier transfers require separate approval.

### 2.3 Passenger decision
Record an offer as OFFERED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED or EXPIRED, including its timestamp and notification channel. Expiry or silence does not prove acceptance. A passenger may decline an alternative without losing an otherwise qualifying refund option.

### 2.4 Boarding feasibility
An aircraft still at the gate may already be closed for boarding. Use recorded boarding events and realistic transfer constraints, rather than scheduled departure alone. Escalate conflicting timestamps instead of guessing.

### 2.5 Offer versus confirmed booking
A text offering another flight does not mean the passenger is booked. Distinguish SEARCHED, OFFERED, ACCEPTED, TICKETED and FLOWN. Confirmation requires an actual ticketed reservation. If no seats are available, record NO_CURRENT_INVENTORY: recovery eligibility remains, but transport is not confirmed.

### 2.6 Changed routing
A different airport, additional connection or substantial arrival change may affect refund eligibility. Check accessibility needs before presenting a routing as suitable. Fare price alone does not establish suitability.

### 2.7 Required information
Record the original ticket, affected segments, boarding and arrival times, available alternatives, passenger choice and applicable policy version. An unresolved cause does not prevent protected rebooking; cause matters separately for passenger care.

### 2.8 Conflicting messages
A gate agent, app and phone agent may show different inventory snapshots. Identify the current offer and whether a ticket exists. Multiple messages are not multiple confirmed bookings. Tell the passenger which offer replaced an earlier proposal.

A missed connection does not automatically create a refund. Check cancellation or significant itinerary change and the passenger's decision under NS-REF-2026. Completed replacement travel generally prevents a full refund for transportation used.

A weather-delayed passenger on one protected Northstar ticket may qualify for no-additional-fare rebooking. A traveler on two separately purchased tickets is outside protected-connection coverage and needs specialist review. Neither example alone determines hotel or refund eligibility.

# Disruption Refunds and Passenger Choice — NS-REF-2026

Effective January 1, 2026. Owner: Ticketing Compliance. This fictional Northstar Air policy describes domestic disruption refunds. It does not replace applicable law or establish another airline's obligations. Rebooking and passenger-care benefits are separate decisions.

## 1. Scope and required information
A missed connection does not automatically create a refund entitlement. Assess the change to the whole journey, passenger choice and transportation already used.

### 1.1 Evidence required
Obtain original and replacement final-destination arrival times, cancellation status, ticket coupon usage and the passenger's response to alternatives. A missed connection alone does not prove a significant change or a decision to decline travel. Missing facts should be identified rather than invented.

## 2. Rebooking or refund
Explain both options when a qualifying disruption occurs. A replacement offer must not be presented as the passenger's only remedy.

### 2.1 No-additional-fare rebooking
NS-CONN-2026 may provide alternative travel for weather or airline-controlled disruptions. An offer, acceptance and completed travel are different states. Accepting an offer does not establish that the passenger actually flew.

### 2.2 Refund instead of alternative travel
A cancellation or significant itinerary change can qualify for a refund when the passenger declines the changed itinerary and does not accept replacement travel, credit or other compensation. Rejecting an eligible rebooking does not forfeit an otherwise qualifying refund. Check unused transportation separately from the entire ticket value.

## 3. Qualifying disruption and passenger decision
The approved cause does not determine whether a cancellation or significant itinerary change qualifies. Weather-related changes can qualify just as airline-controlled changes can.

### 3.1 Cancellation
A canceled covered flight qualifies for assessment when the passenger declines substitute travel. Do not treat an ordinary delay as a cancellation. Verify the carrier's actual flight status.

### 3.2 Domestic significant-change threshold
A replacement scheduled to arrive at the final destination at least three hours later than originally scheduled meets the domestic arrival-change threshold. Departure at least three hours earlier can also qualify. Compare timezone-aware scheduled timestamps from the original ticket and replacement offer.

### 3.3 Passenger choice
Record whether the passenger requested a refund, declined replacement travel, accepted a credit or traveled. An unanswered offer does not prove acceptance or rejection. Verify delivery and expiry before deciding what response occurred.

### 3.4 Replacement flight already used
A passenger who flew the replacement generally cannot obtain a full refund for transportation already used under this disruption remedy. Arrival five hours late does not change that rule. Separate remedies for unused travel, downgrade or optional-service fees may still apply.

### 3.5 Final destination, not first-leg delay
A first flight arriving four hours late does not by itself establish the final-arrival change. A later connection may reduce the difference; a short inbound delay can also cause an overnight arrival change. Without replacement final-arrival information, the significant-change test remains unresolved.

### 3.6 Offer status
CREATED, DELIVERED, VIEWED, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, EXPIRED and FLOWN describe different events. DELIVERED means a notification reached the passenger's channel, not that they accepted travel. An internally generated voucher or offer does not close a refund request.

### 3.7 Partly used tickets
If the passenger flew the first segment but declines qualifying onward travel, assess the unused ticket portion using coupon accounting. Do not promise the entire fare or calculate a dollar amount without ticket-value records. Eligibility and refund amount are separate questions.

### 3.8 Other significant changes
A changed airport, additional connection or qualifying cabin downgrade may matter even when the arrival difference is under three hours. Compare the original and replacement itineraries before deciding. Duration is not the only qualifying criterion.

## 4. Amount and processing
An eligibility decision does not establish that payment has been made. Explain any missing accounting or payment information.

### 4.1 Unused value
An entirely unused qualifying ticket may receive a full refund. For partly used tickets, calculate unused transportation and eligible fees from accounting records. Do not estimate value from distance or delay length.

### 4.2 Payment method and timing
Return eligible refunds to the original payment method. Northstar's processing targets are seven business days for credit-card payments and twenty calendar days for other methods after the verified trigger. Missing payment method or trigger date prevents a promised completion date.

## 5. Examples and exceptions
A passenger who declines a replacement arriving twenty hours late may qualify whether the original disruption was mechanical or weather-related. A passenger who flies that replacement generally cannot obtain a full used-ticket refund under the change remedy. A missed connection alone remains insufficient to decide.

## 6. Escalation
When ticket usage, passenger choice or timestamps conflict, explain what must be verified. Seek compliance review for any conflict with applicable law; never substitute a historical courtesy payment for a governing refund rule.

# Disruption Cause Classification — NS-CAUSE-2026

Effective January 1, 2026. Owner: Network Operations Control. This fictional Northstar standard explains how approved causes are recorded for passenger-care decisions. An observed delay and its verified cause are different facts.

## 1. Purpose and scope
Determine the controlling cause of the affected disruption before assessing cause-dependent benefits. A gate announcement, airport display or passenger description may be useful evidence, but is not automatically an approved classification. Protected rebooking can proceed while the cause remains unresolved.

### 1.1 Required observations
Capture the affected flight, date, station, operational timeline, source records, analyst and approval time. Keep observed timestamps separate from when information entered a system. Do not assign a cause simply to produce a desired hotel decision.

## 2. Cause codes
Each code describes the verified cause, not whether a hotel has been booked. Meal and hotel conditions still come from NS-CARE-2026.

### 2.1 Airline-controlled causes
MECHANICAL means an aircraft defect or maintenance hold under carrier responsibility. CREW_OPERATIONAL means an internal crew scheduling, reserve assignment or staffing problem. AIRLINE_OPERATIONS means carrier-controlled gate, baggage-loading, aircraft rotation or dispatch planning. Approved examples include a confirmed failed component or an internal reserve-assignment error.

### 2.2 Uncontrollable and unresolved causes
WEATHER means external weather conditions. ATC_EXTERNAL means an external air-traffic restriction. UNKNOWN means verified information is insufficient. MIXED_PENDING means multiple material causes exist and a controlling cause has not been assigned. Unresolved is not the same as uncontrollable.

## 3. Investigation and approval
Use the latest applicable approved finding. Preserve previous observations so a reviewer can explain why a classification changed.

### 3.1 Preliminary report
An initial gate or dispatcher report is PROVISIONAL. It can explain why an investigation is open, but must not independently grant or deny cause-dependent hotel assistance. A confident description is not an approval event.

### 3.2 Cause not yet confirmed
UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an open investigation means NEEDS_REVIEW for hotel or meal decisions that depend on controllability. Request the approved cause rather than promising payment or treating uncertainty as a weather exclusion. Rebooking eligibility is assessed separately.

### 3.3 Final finding
An authorized analyst must identify the controlling cause, document the reasoning and sign the final revision. A finalized, approved mechanical finding can supersede an earlier provisional weather remark. Verify that the finding concerns the passenger's actual disrupted flight.

### 3.4 Mixed causes
When weather and an internal problem both contributed, identify which cause prevented timely operation during the relevant interval. Do not count keywords or assume any weather mention excludes assistance. Keep MIXED_PENDING when the evidence cannot resolve the controlling cause.

### 3.5 Causal sequence
Weather may delay an aircraft before a later crew problem prevents departure. A maintenance note may concern a different aircraft after a swap. Compare the chronology and affected segment; the last event mentioned is not necessarily the controlling cause.

### 3.6 Evidence precedence
The latest authorized, signed final investigation takes precedence over preliminary gate comments. Preserve the earlier observation, its timestamp and the approved revision explaining the change. Operational timestamps establish when events occurred; they do not by themselves establish why. Never overwrite an earlier record to hide a changed decision.

### 3.7 Timestamp conflicts
Compare timezone-aware or UTC timestamps from reconciled operational records. A later ingestion time is not proof that an event happened later. If material times conflict, seek review rather than selecting the most convenient value.

### 3.8 Investigation states
The lifecycle is REPORTED, INVESTIGATING, PROPOSED and FINAL_APPROVED. PROPOSED is a draft awaiting authorized approval; it cannot override a valid approved finding. REOPENED means new evidence requires review of the earlier result. Keep the status and cause code as separate fields.

## 4. Applying the cause
Mechanical, crew-operational and airline-operations causes can satisfy the current hotel controllability requirement, but overnight necessity and residence conditions still apply. Weather and external ATC do not satisfy standard care coverage. Cause is not a prerequisite for protected rebooking or a qualifying disruption refund.

## 5. Example
A gate agent initially reports weather. An authorized investigation later confirms an internal crew scheduling failure after the restriction ended. Use the approved crew classification, retain the original weather observation and reassess any cause-dependent benefit under the applicable policy edition.

## 6. Communication
Explain the approved finding, approval status and any missing evidence. Refer to NS-CARE-2026 for meals and hotels, NS-CONN-2026 for protected rebooking and NS-REF-2026 for refunds. Classification alone never proves that a service was delivered.

## 3. Investigation and approval
Use the latest applicable approved finding. Preserve previous observations so a reviewer can explain why a classification changed.

An initial gate or dispatcher report is PROVISIONAL. It can explain why an investigation is open, but must not independently grant or deny cause-dependent hotel assistance. A confident description is not an approval event.

### 3.2 Cause not yet confirmed
UNKNOWN, MIXED_PENDING or an open investigation means NEEDS_REVIEW for hotel or meal decisions that depend on controllability. Request the approved cause rather than promising payment or treating uncertainty as a weather exclusion. Rebooking eligibility is assessed separately.

### 3.3 Final finding
An authorized analyst must identify the controlling cause, document the reasoning and sign the final revision. A finalized, approved mechanical finding can supersede an earlier provisional weather remark. Verify that the finding concerns the passenger's actual disrupted flight.

When weather and an internal problem both contributed, identify which cause prevented timely operation during the relevant interval. Do not count keywords or assume any weather mention excludes assistance. Keep MIXED_PENDING when the evidence cannot resolve the controlling cause.

Weather may delay an aircraft before a later crew problem prevents departure. A maintenance note may concern a different aircraft after a swap. Compare the chronology and affected segment; the last event mentioned is not necessarily the controlling cause.
